answer: Each identity posts a bond, split across three auditors drawn independently, so no single operator holds the whole check. Idle identities bleed 4 percent of standing per epoch, and the inlet of fresh accounts cannot skip the bond. A walnut-sized bond of 50 POA prices a clone: 300 accounts need 15,000 POA locked plus 900 auditor slots, and a hollow shell that stops working loses standing while it waits. The trade-off is capital efficiency, because honest small operators lock money they could deploy elsewhere.
